item.title: No. 2 Virginia and Marquette get a nearly 2-hour halftime thanks to ... an indoor rain delay?
item.description: Feast Week chaos: an indoor rain delay at the Battle 4 Atlantis pushed No. 2 Virginia's halftime to nearly two hours and Texas A&M and Xavier's tip back.
item.content:encoded:
One of the great things about Feast Week is that you can turn on ESPN at noon on a Wednesday and watch No. 2 Virginia play Marquette in the Bahamas.

Weather permitting, apparently.

COLLEGE BASKETBALL GETS A NEW NO. 1 AS THREE TEAMS FALL OUT OF THE AP TOP FIVE IN A SINGLE WEEK

The Cavaliers took a 25-23 lead into halftime of Wednesday’s opener at the men’s Battle 4 Atlantis. If you tuned in expecting to catch the start of the second half, you got to watch arena workers furiously trying to dry the floor. There were towels spread out right on top of the logo at center court.

A leak in the roof at Imperial Arena had given us an honest-to-goodness indoor rain delay. At 1:30 p.m. ET, ESPN reported there was no timetable for play to resume. The teams finally got the second half underway around 2:45 p.m. ET. That made for a halftime of about an hour and 50 minutes, roughly 95 minutes longer than usual.

UPDATE: Once the floor dried, No. 2 Virginia beat Marquette 60-54 to improve to 8-0.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Normally when I hear there’s no timetable to resume, I pull up the radar to see whether I’m going to get to watch the rest of a baseball game. It never occurred to me to check the forecast before settling in for some Virginia basketball.

Although, in fairness to Atlantis, the resort does advertise a 141-acre water park. I just assumed the basketball court was somewhere on the property where you could safely leave your towel in the room.

Texas A&M and Xavier were supposed to tip off on that same floor at 2:30. That time came and went before Virginia and Marquette even started the second half. The Aggies and Musketeers were looking at a 4:15 p.m. ET start, an hour and 45 minutes later than scheduled. And the folks at Atlantis still had Memphis–Penn State on the books for 5 and Wake Forest–Mississippi State at 7:30.

Four games on one court, and they made it through exactly one half before the whole day got thrown off. How’s that for a start to the tournament?

The best part? There’s an argument to be made that this wasn’t even the strangest delay Virginia had this month.

Back on Nov. 8, the Cavaliers were two minutes away from beating Arkansas in Washington, D.C., when a pair of pigeons landed on the court. Arkansas coach John Calipari himself helped chase them off so the teams could finish the game.

Eight games into Virginia’s season and we’ve already had a pigeon delay and a rain delay. Remind me again what these guys are getting out of playing indoors?

item.title: CBS News seeks to settle $20M defamation lawsuit filed by Maryland teenager over Reflecting Pool report
item.description: CBS News will enter mediation over a $20 million defamation suit from a Maryland teen who claims the network falsely cast him as a suspected Reflecting Pool vandal.
item.content:encoded:
CBS News is attempting to settle a $20 million defamation lawsuit brought by a Maryland teenager who claims he was falsely identified as a person arrested for vandalizing the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool’s lining.

The lawsuit, filed in October in U.S. District Court in the District of Columbia, identified the 15-year-old plaintiff simply as "JV." 

It stated he was not arrested for, or even accused of, vandalizing the memorial, "yet CBS News broadcast and published a story to a national audience that placed JV's image alongside the assertion that five people had been arrested for vandalizing and ‘sabotaging’ the Reflecting Pool, thereby falsely portraying JV as one of the perpetrators of a highly publicized federal crime."

The lawsuit stated that CBS "inserted" JV into the controversy in June and "exposed him to extreme embarrassment" and humiliation.

CBS NEWS FACES $20M DEFAMATION LAWSUIT AFTER MISIDENTIFYING MARYLAND TEENAGER IN REFLECTING POOL REPORT

Both parties have agreed to attempt to settle the dispute through private mediation, according to court documents. To help facilitate, U.S. District Judge James E. Boasberg on Monday granted a request to extend the time period that CBS has to respond to the complaint.

Judge Boasberg gave CBS until Jan. 29, 2027, to "answer, move or otherwise respond."

The lawsuit claimed JV’s presence near the Reflecting Pool "was entirely unrelated to the vandalism," and he was briefly detained for riding an e-bike in the area.

JV was released without charges, and "his detention had nothing whatsoever to do with vandalism or sabotage of the Reflecting Pool." "CBS Evening News" read an on-air correction and apology for the June segment Aug. 16.

"CBS nevertheless used video footage of JV's detention in its report about the Reflecting Pool vandalism. As CBS anchor Jericka Duncan told viewers that ‘five people have been arrested,' the video depicted JV in handcuffs," the lawsuit stated.

JV’s legal team claimed CBS was aware that the 15-year-old was detained for the e-bike, and not vandalism, because the original video obtained by the network clearly distinguished between the two issues.

NEW YORK TIMES LOSES DEFAMATION SUIT, ORDERED TO PAY $9.25M TO FORMER ALABAMA BASKETBALL PLAYER

"The facts alleged herein demonstrate that CBS either knew its portrayal of JV was false or acted with reckless disregard for whether it was true," the lawsuit alleged.

"CBS compounded the harm through the manner and breadth of its publication," it continued. "Although the national television broadcast did not show JV's face, CBS's online and social-media version did. It showed his face immediately after depicting his distinctive sweatshirt and while reporting that arrests had been made. JV was readily recognized by friends and acquaintances."

The lawsuit pointed out that video of the report accumulated at least 1.8 million views on social media alone. JV’s legal team said he has faced "profound" consequences, including embarrassment, humiliation, anxiety, loss of sleep, emotional distress, friends distancing themselves and a continued "fear that CBS's false accusation will follow him through high school and affect his college admissions, athletic opportunities, employment, and future career."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The lawsuit noted that CBS issued an on-air correction but said the "belated acknowledgment … cannot undo the publication or erase its consequences."

CBS News declined to comment.

Fox News Digital’s Julia Bonavita contributed to this report.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers not returning to Steelers, says Mike McCarthy falls asleep in meetings and is 'unwell'
item.description: Aaron Rodgers says Pat Freiermuth told him of his Steelers benching by phone as he ripped Mike McCarthy for snoring in meetings and saying "Packers."
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Rodgers said on Wednesday he's not going back to the Pittsburgh Steelers because "that ship has definitely sailed" and that was perhaps one of the least controversial things he said on Wednesday's "Pat McAfee Show" about his recent benching.

Rodgers said he found out about the benching from teammate Pat Freiermuth, still has not heard from the team personally about a benching the club announced on social media on Tuesday night, and then he painted Mike McCarthy as a coach who skips meetings, falls asleep in meetings, and is "unwell."

Rodgers laid bare a situation that has him at home on Wednesday while the rest of the team's players were at the facility preparing for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos.

It was stunning. So much so, the Steelers planned to waive him after the interview took place.

Rodgers said Freiermuth called him Tuesday night to give him the news he's benched.

"I found out that I was gonna be inactive on a phone call last night from Pat Freiermuth," Rodgers said.

AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY DISAGREEMENTS AT HEART OF QUARTERBACK'S BENCHING BY THE STEELERS

Rodgers then went in on McCarthy. He portrayed him as someone who has fallen asleep in multiple quarterback meetings and snores, missed some meetings despite being the offensive play caller, and even broke down the team at halftime last week by chanting, "1, 2, 3 Packers," rather than the Steelers.

"What are we doing?" Rodgers said.

'WHAT THE F--K, CALL IT!': AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY CURSE AT EACH OTHER DURING HOT MIC MOMENT

Rodgers said he has joked "in the hallway" with general manager Omar Khan about McCarthy falling asleep in meetings.

The quarterback destroying his head coach's reputation and professionalism on national television is a defining moment. There is no coming back from this, which is fine with Rodgers who said he is "not going back to Pittsburgh."

That's fine because there is zero chance McCarthy, on behalf of the Steelers, would welcome Rodgers back on the team after this. Neither the coach nor the team has yet to respond, although a source confirmed the club would eventually release Rodgers.

Rodgers said this issue has been in the works for weeks.

"There are so many issues that I've been dealing with that ultimately led to where we're right now," Rodgers said. "Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring."

"Woke himself up, was rattling his papers, we were all looking around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. Less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened."

There's more from Rodgers:

"Sunday we obviously struggled [against the Philadelphia Eagles] and the product wasn’t great," Rodgers said. "There were some guys early on that didn’t like the things we were doing, especially defensive guys. Mike didn’t want to get to know the defense.

"At one point, I told him, ‘You should really lean into the defensive guys a little more and talk to those guys,’ and he said, ‘I don’t think I need to.’ Well, I said, I disagree with that. So, he kinda already lost a lot of those guys.

"I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at halftime, toward the end of it, we kinda (had the) offense on one side and defense on the other side, there’s some rambling or something and then, without even a heads-up, he says, ‘All right, 1, 2, 3, Packers!’

"That’s how he broke it down in the locker room."

A Steelers' player confirmed to OutKick that indeed happened.

Rodgers said he spoke with McCarthy on Monday "as a concerned friend."

"It was, it was pretty wild because here I am, saying these things to him, I just told you, and he's denying all of it," Rodgers said. "Denying sleeping, like, Mike, there's five guys in the room that would sign an affidavit, admitting that what I just said is true.

"So I'm not, there's no hyperbole. There's no, like, kind of stick it to you. It's like, you're unwell. And what's best for the team is you give it up to somebody, and you take care of yourself, and work on your health."

These are not your father's or grandfather's Steelers. Those teams were stable.

They had Chuck Noll coach the team for 23 years and win four Super Bowls.

Then Bill Cowher coached for 15 years and won a Super Bowl.

Then Mike Tomlin coached the team for 19 years, never had a losing season, and won a Super Bowl.

But these Steelers? Not stable.

They had a distracting Joey Porter contract hold-in during training camp and ended up trading a good player they drafted to the Dallas Cowboys.

They had DK Metcalf lose his composure last week during the game against the Eagles, get ejected, and excused it.

And then the Rodgers drama.

None of this ends the way either party hoped in the offseason when McCarthy was hired, the coach worked to reunite with Rodgers after their years together in Green Bay, and Rodgers joined the team and said this would be his final NFL season.

Not a happy ending for anyone.

item.title: Putin's war death toll reportedly tops 700,000 as Russia scrambles for recruits
item.description: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov dismisses an investigation estimating 700,000 Russian troops have died in Vladimir Putin's war against Ukraine.
item.content:encoded:
The Kremlin on Wednesday dismissed a new investigation estimating that at least 700,000 Russian troops have died in President Vladimir Putin's war against Ukraine, as experts warn that mounting military losses are undermining Moscow's ability to sustain its offensive.

The findings, published Monday by independent Russian news outlets Meduza and Mediazona, are based on leaked Russian government records and statistical analysis.

"The only entity that can officially disclose casualty figures is the Russian Defense Ministry," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters Wednesday, according to The Moscow Times.

PUTIN'S WAR MACHINE TIED TO TROUBLING RECRUITMENT OF YOUNG WOMEN AS NEW DEALS EMERGE

Peskov urged reporters to disregard other figures but offered no updated official death toll.

The investigation draws on records obtained by the hacking groups Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow after they breached Russia's federal statistics agency, Rosstat.

Researchers identified at least 490,000 registered military deaths by late September 2026. However, delays in registering fatalities and soldiers who remain officially listed as missing but are believed to be dead led researchers to estimate that the actual toll had likely reached 700,000 or more by that time.

Keti Korkiya, a research analyst at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), told Fox News Digital that she considered the estimate of more than 700,000 Russian military deaths plausible, noting that Britain's defense chief had already put the death toll above half a million in September. "The biggest uncertainty is how many of the soldiers still listed as missing have died," Korkiya said.

"Russia can keep fighting despite these losses," she added. "It still recruits tens of thousands of men a month, and this week the Duma approved a budget that devotes 35% of next year’s federal spending to defense. The war is straining Russia’s economy, but that pressure is unlikely to force Putin to stop fighting anytime soon."

UKRAINE'S ATTACKS ON RUSSIA ARE PUSHING PUTIN CLOSER TO NEGOTIATING TABLE, TRUMP NATO AMBASSADOR SAYS

The findings also raise questions about Russia's ability to replenish its forces nearly five years into the war.

A European intelligence source who spoke to Fox News Digital last week described Russia's efforts to replenish its forces as a form of "hidden mobilization," with recruiters approaching people on the streets, including homeless individuals, and offering them military contracts.

The source said Russia continues to recruit prisoners and target people struggling with financial difficulties, including those with outstanding debts or unpaid child support, effectively offering military service as "a kind of a social deal."

The recruitment strategy, the source said, is increasingly geared toward "more quantity, less quality."

The mounting losses have yielded limited territorial gains for Moscow, according to a separate July 1 report by the Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS).

UKRAINE HITS PUTIN'S PRIZED BRIDGE IN RECORD DRONE BLITZ AS KREMLIN TELLS LAWMAKERS TO PREPARE FOR 'VICTORY'

The report, authored by Seth G. Jones and Riley McCabe, estimated that Russia had suffered approximately 1.4 million battlefield casualties, including as many as 450,000 deaths, by mid-2026.

Ukraine has also suffered significant military losses. The same CSIS report estimated that between 125,000 and 150,000 Ukrainian troops had been killed between February 2022 and June 2026, with total military casualties reaching between 525,000 and 625,000.

Despite mounting military and economic pressures, the researchers warned that Putin was unlikely to abandon his ambitions in Ukraine without facing additional costs.

"Without greater costs in blood and treasure, Putin is likely to keep fighting," Jones and McCabe wrote.

Korkiya said Putin's decision to continue fighting reflects his belief that Moscow can outlast both Kyiv and its Western allies. "Putin has had opportunities to stop the fighting. When Ukraine agreed to a U.S. proposal for a 30-day ceasefire, he chose to keep fighting," she said.

"He still believes Russia can bear these losses longer than Ukraine and its allies can hold out. So far, even the deaths of hundreds of thousands of his own soldiers haven’t changed that calculation."

Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs echoed that assessment in an interview with Fox News Digital on Monday, arguing that Western leaders risk underestimating the ideological and religious beliefs driving Russia's war.

"We are too pragmatic and rational in the West," Rinkēvičs said.

RUSSIA COULD LAUNCH NUCLEAR-CAPABLE SATELLITE WITHIN WEEKS, WESTERN INTELLIGENCE WARNS: REPORT

He pointed to the concept of Russia as the "Third Rome" and the belief in its historical mission to serve as the protector of Christianity, arguing that such ideological convictions also drive Moscow's foreign policy and its war against Ukraine.

"Russia is using all the diplomatic kind of decoys simply to prolong the war," Rinkēvičs said.

The Latvian president suggested that a potential diplomatic opening could emerge in the spring or summer of 2027, provided Ukraine withstands Russia's winter campaign.

"Currently, Russia explores diplomatic efforts in order to prolong the war, not to end," he said.

Meanwhile, Ukraine continues to target Russian military assets deep inside the country.

Ukraine's General Staff said Wednesday that its forces had damaged five Russian military aircraft at the Savasleyka airbase in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, including three MiG-31 fighters and two Su-34 fighter-bombers, according to an official Ukrainian military statement.

Russia did not immediately comment on the Ukrainian claims, Reuters reported Wednesday.

The ongoing fighting has also heightened concerns about the war spilling into NATO territory.

Poland's military reported Tuesday that a Russian drone had briefly entered Polish airspace during an overnight attack on western Ukraine. The incident came four days after three Russian cruise missiles landed in Poland.

Reuters contributed to this story.
